| OQ-1170 | **THE MOMENT WE CALL A CUT ACCOUNT `Disconnected`, IT LEAVES THE BILL RUN — SO WHO BILLS THE DAYS IT USED BEFORE THE CUT, AND WHAT DOES IT COME BACK AS?** Plainly, with the figure: **`A-11488` is cut on 18 August owing $612.75.** It used water and electricity from the 1st to the 18th and nobody has billed those eighteen days yet — that bill goes out in September. BR-CUS-107 says a cut account is `Disconnected`, and the moment that word is written on the account it drops out of the September run: the run asks `customers.selectors.accounts_for_bill_run` who to bill, that read answers *the accounts that occupy a unit*, and a disconnected account no longer occupies one (BR-CUS-110, ruled 26 August). **So the eighteen days are billed to nobody** — not to this customer, and not to whoever moves in next, because their bill starts on their move-in day. On a **$40.00** monthly base that is **$23.23** of base already served (18 days of 31), plus every gallon and every kWh recorded in those eighteen days. ⚠ **THIS IS NOT A NEW RULE — IT IS TWO SIGNED RULES MEETING.** BR-CUS-103 (PO 2026-08-25, *"no"* to base running on after a cut) says in its own words: *"a service is billed base right up to the moment it is cut, because until then it was available"*. That works TODAY only because a cut account is still billable and still in the run; BR-CUS-107 takes it out of the run. One of the two has to give and the supersession must be STATED, never assumed. **Options: (A) BILL THE CUT CYCLE FIRST, THEN CALL IT DISCONNECTED** — the status is written when the cycle containing the cut has been billed, not on the day of the cut. Costs no money and leaves the account reading its old status for up to a month after the service is off, which is DEF-701's complaint still on the screen. · **(B) RAISE THE FINAL METERED BILL AT THE CUT**, for the period start up to and including the cut day, and write the status straight away. Correct money and a correct pill on the day; it is a new act at the cut, and `DSC-02.4` is explicit that a cut *"leaves the account open"* and is *"not a move-out"*, so the act must be a bill and nothing else. · **(C) LET A DISCONNECTED ACCOUNT STAY IN THE RUN UNTIL ITS LAST SERVED DAY IS BILLED** — customers keeps answering with it and billing learns to bill a `non_billable` account for a closed window. Most faithful to both rules, biggest change, and it reaches into billing. **Eng leans (B)**: it is the only one that gets the money and the screen right on the same day, and the product already raises a bill at the cut for the **$75.00** reconnection fee, so the door exists. **Not chosen — the prime directive forbids it.** ⚠ **AND A SECOND HALF, SMALLER AND JUST AS SHARP: WHAT STATUS DOES A RESTORED ACCOUNT GO BACK TO?** `restore_service` writes the reconnection date and touches no account column, so an account made `Disconnected` at the cut is STILL `Disconnected` after the crew turns the water back on — **outside every bill run, for ever, silently.** Nothing signed says whether it returns to `Active`, to `Marked disconnect` (it may still owe), or to something else. Both halves must be ruled in the same breath, or task 1 ships a customer who is reconnected and never billed again. **Measured, not argued:** `06-backend/tests/test_cr052_w0_disconnected_at_the_cut.py` — `test_the_days_before_the_cut_are_billed_by_nobody` and `test_restoring_writes_no_account_status`. | product | CR-052 W0 lane, 2026-08-30 | **CR-052 tasks 1 and 2 · DEF-701** — now UNBLOCKED | **CLOSED 2026-08-30 ✅ — NEITHER OPTION AS OFFERED: THE PO WIDENED IT.** Verbatim: *"when we disconnect - we generate final bill at that time itself - so later bill is not required ... entire workflow including all settlement and status update is taken care at time of disconnect or move out - so account status changes and outstanding is pending on account if any"*. **The cut is the WHOLE event** — final bill, settlement and status, all at the cut; there is no later bill; any remainder stays outstanding on the account. **So neither signed rule gives way:** BR-CUS-103 keeps its words exactly (base runs to the moment of the cut) because those days are now billed AT the cut rather than a month later, and BR-CUS-107 writes `Disconnected` immediately because nothing is left for the next run to do. The collision was an artefact of billing LATE and the ruling removes the lateness. **SECOND HALF DECIDED, NOT RE-ASKED (law 13):** a restored account returns to the billable status it held before the cut. Derived, not invented — `disconnects.mark_reconnecting` refuses with `not_settled` while the account owes and records `settled_balance` on success, so a case reaches RECONNECTING → RESTORED only once the balance is clear; the debt that would justify `Marked disconnect` cannot exist at that point. Full reasoning in the decision log, 2026-08-30. ⛔ **THAT DERIVATION DIED ON 2026-09-25 AND THE CONCLUSION IS LEFT STANDING WITHOUT IT — READ THIS BEFORE BUILDING FROM THE SECOND HALF.** `BR-CUS-1097` (PO 2026-09-25, verbatim: *"Show what's still owed and let the clerk proceed"*) supersedes `BR-CUS-104`'s clear-before-reconnecting gate, so **a restored account CAN owe money** and `mark_reconnecting` refusing with `not_settled` is no longer law. The sentence above — *"a case reaches RECONNECTING → RESTORED only once the balance is clear"* — is FALSE, and with it the reason `Marked disconnect` was ruled out. **The conclusion (a restored account returns to the billable status it held before the cut) is NOT reversed here and is not re-opened; it is now UNARGUED**, and whoever next touches restored status must re-argue it on its own facts rather than cite this. A justification by reference outlives the justification. ## OQ-387 — is "a unit's services are its premises' services" a DERIVATION or an INVARIANT?

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-26 by lane UNITSVC's measurement, immediately
after the PO withdrew CR-037 and set the rule *"premises services = Unit
services"*.

**Why it is a real question and not a detail.** The rule can be built two ways
and they behave differently on data that already exists:

| Reading | What it means | What it costs |
|---|---|---|
| **A · A READ-TIME DERIVATION** — the unit screens show the PREMISES' list | one place changes (`unit_list_dict`); nothing about existing data has to be true | ⚠ **unusable until DEF-756 is fixed**: no screen can write a premises' services, so every hand-built premises has NONE, and its units would show no services while genuinely holding meters |
| **B · AN INVARIANT the write paths enforce** — `ensure_service_point` refuses a service the premises does not offer | the equality becomes a property the code holds, not an assumption about data | four write paths gain a refusal (the unit wizard's meter grid, the assets lane, the importer, W6 connections), and **existing tenants may already violate it** |

**MEASURED, 2026-08-26 — the facts either answer rests on:**

1. **Nothing enforces the equality at any layer today.** `ensure_service_point`
   and `_clean_services` validate against the **tenant-enabled** set only, never
   against the premises' list. A unit can acquire `gas` at a premises whose list
   is `["water","sewer"]`, through any of four paths.
2. **Every unit-services read goes through `ServicePoint`; not one reads
   `premises.services_available`** (DEF-755).
3. **`premises.services_available` is writable by no screen** (DEF-756).
4. **A disconnection already breaks the equality**: `service_points_for` filters
   `deleted_at__isnull=True`, so pulling a meter removes the service from every
   unit screen, the service-agreement path and the billing gather — while the
   premises list is untouched. **This is the inversion CR-037's own text warned
   about, and it exists WITHOUT CR-037.**
5. **The demo tenant hides all of it** — the seeders write the same list by hand
   to the premises AND to each unit, so they agree in seeded data and can only
   diverge in an imported or UI-built tenant.

**To put to the PO in plain English, with the case that decides it:** *a clerk
adds `500 Main St` by hand today and the product never asks which services it
has. Its units have water and sewer meters fitted. Under reading A the unit
screens would show **no services at all**; under reading B nothing changes on
screen but a future gas meter would be refused until someone edits the address.*
Neither is what a clerk expects, which is why DEF-756 is the precondition for
either.

## OQ-388 — should a premises row whose address is already on file be SKIPPED under `Insert new only`?

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-26 by lane IMPORTTRUTH, which stopped at it
rather than decide it.

**The concrete case.** A utility imports a file in **`Insert new only`**. One row
carries `500 Main St`, and a premises is already on file at that address.

| Answer | What happens | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Skip it** | the row is not loaded and the receipt says so | ⚠ the product **silently does not load a row the operator handed us**. That is the mirror image of the write-nobody-asked-for that `PRM.TYPE_IN_LOOKUP` refuses two entries below it in the same file, and BR-MET-090 exists because *"a warning that PERFORMS A WRITE the operator never asked for"* is the shape to avoid |
| **B · Load it and warn** (what happens today) | a second premises is created at the same address, flagged | duplicate addresses, which is what the rule was written to prevent |

**What is already settled and is NOT this question.** Under **`Insert & update`**
the answer is certain and needs no ruling: *already on file* is the **expected
state of every row** — that is what the mode is FOR — so a skip there would
strand the operator's whole file a second time. `PRM.ADDRESS_ON_FILE` is
therefore `flag_only` today (DEF-750), and no row loads differently than it did
before; the product simply stopped **promising** a skip it never performed.

**⚠ IT CANNOT BE BUILT YET EVEN IF RULED A.** The run does not carry
`write_mode` until the load, so stage 3 cannot judge a rule against the chosen
mode. That is **CR-036 (g)'s remaining half** — the control moved to stage 1 and
the verdict is *reported under* the mode, not *re-scored by* it. So this question
can be answered now and acted on later, in that order.

## OQ-394 — a move-out's final read: does the prior final read PRE-FILL the input, or only sit under it as help text?

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-26 by lane W9 (CR-038), which BUILT one of the
two answers and is flagging that it chose rather than followed a rule.

**The concrete case.** A clerk opens the move-out wizard for unit 12B. The meter's
last committed reading is **42,864 kWh**, taken eight days ago. The clerk has to
enter the FINAL read.

| Answer | What the clerk sees | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Pre-fill the input with 42,864** | the field opens with a number in it, ready to accept or overwrite | ⚠ **a meter reading nobody took becomes the reading of record by inaction.** A clerk in a hurry presses Next, and 42,864 — eight days stale — closes the account, bills the final invoice, and is what the next occupant's opening read is measured from. Consumption for those eight days is billed as **zero** |
| **B · Empty input, prior read in the help line** (what W9 BUILT) | *"Last read 42,864 kWh on 2026-08-18"* under an empty field | the clerk types the number every time, including when the meter genuinely has not moved. Slower, and BR-CUS-021 can be read as asking for the pre-fill |

**What W9 did and why it is REPORTED rather than assumed.** The lane read
BR-CUS-021 as ambiguous on this point and built **B**, on the reasoning above:
a pre-filled meter reading is a figure no human observed, and the move-out read
is the one number on the screen that decides a final bill. That is a judgment
where the rules ran out, not a rule the lane was given — which is exactly the
case CLAUDE.md's write-back rule says goes in the register before the code is
reported as done.

**⚠ IT IS BUILT EITHER WAY, so this is cheap to reverse.** If the PO rules A,
the change is one default value in `MoveOutWizard` plus its DOM test; no
migration, no data, no money rule. The ledger row for
`customers/0026_cr038_w9_final_read_state.py` carries the same flag.

## OQ-395 — `makemigrations --check` is claimed in every lane report and run by no gate

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-26 by the CR-038 merge lane, alongside DEF-801.

**What happened.** `makemigrations --check` was RED on this branch — the
autodetector wanted `+ Create model Transfer` — and every lane report on it
carries `makemigrations --check✔` in its `gates:` line. Both statements were
made honestly. The check is a **sentence a human types into a report**, and
`10-scripts/run_gates.sh` does not run it, so nothing ever compared the claim to
the command. DEF-801 fixed the migration; it did not fix that.

**The question is not whether to add it — it is what it costs.**

| Answer | What it takes | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Add `makemigrations --check --dry-run` to `run_gates.sh`** | one command; it needs `django.setup()` and the URLconf, ~4s | ⚠ **it will be red the first time somebody legitimately adds a model and lands the migration in a second commit**, which is a normal shape in this repo's lanes. A gate that is red for correct work gets ignored, and an ignored gate is DEF-805 again |
| **B · Add it as a test in `06-backend/tests/`** | same command, inside pytest, so it runs where lanes already look | slower to notice (it is one test among thousands) but it fails the SUITE, which lanes cannot report green around |
| **C · Leave it as a report line** | nothing | it has already failed once, silently, for an unknown number of days |

**Recommendation: B.** The failure this is protecting against is not a lane
forgetting to run a command — it is a lane RUNNING it, in a tree where the
result was already red for somebody else's reason, and reading past it. A test
carries the failure into the same output the lane is already reading.

**⚠ This is not the merge lane's to build.** `10-scripts/` and the gate suite
need their own packet, and the same self-test question covers every zero-baseline
ratchet in there (DEF-805). Raised, not chosen.

## OQ-417 — `generation_channel` is switchable and its mirror image is locked

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-26 by the CR-038 BR-MET-136 rule-switch lane,
while building the switch. **Nothing is blocked on it**: the ruling was followed
literally and the rule is switchable today.

**What was ruled.** BR-MET-136 clause 4 names the checks a utility may NEVER
switch off, and it names them one by one: *"The INTEGRITY rules (unknown_meter,
retired_meter, unit_missing, negative_usage, rollover, duplicate,
export_not_net) are NOT switchable."* Seven names. Everything else is a judgment
rule the utility may retire.

**What that leaves.** `generation_channel` (BR-MET-135, ruled the SAME DAY in a
different sitting) is not among the seven, so it is switchable. But look at what
it does beside the rule that IS locked:

| Rule | What it refuses | Severity | Threshold | Switchable today |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `export_not_net` | an EXPORT reading on an asset that is not a net meter | ERROR, no auto-fix | none — it is a fact about the asset | **NO — locked by name** |
| `generation_channel` | a `generation` reading on a METER, or a DEVICE's reading in a consumption register | ERROR, no auto-fix | none — it is a fact about the asset | **YES** |

They are the same shape pointed at opposite equipment, and BR-MET-135's own
words are why: *"a device's produced quantity … distinct from `export` … and
never summed with consumption."* A solar inverter's 612 kWh landing in `total`
is generation being BILLED AS USAGE — a customer's bill, wrong, in their favour
or against.

**The options and what each costs.**

| Answer | What it means | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Lock it — add `generation_channel` to the integrity seven** | a utility can never switch off "a PV inverter's output is not consumption" | one line in `validation.INTEGRITY_RULES` and its test. ⚠ A tenant that has already switched it off would have it silently switched back on — today there is none, so the window is now |
| **B · Leave it switchable (today's state)** | a utility that does not sell solar can retire a check that never fires for them | a utility that DOES sell solar can switch off the only thing standing between an inverter reading and a consumption register. Nothing else catches it: the figure is a valid number in a valid register |
| **C · Lock it only where the tenant sells solar or battery** | the check binds exactly where it can fire | a rule whose LOCKED-ness depends on the enabled service set is a new concept in this engine, and S64 would have to explain why one utility sees a padlock and another sees a checkbox |

**Recommendation: A**, and the reason is the ruling's own logic rather than a
new judgment: the PO locked the seven because a utility must not be able to
switch off a check that protects the DATA rather than expressing a business
preference. `generation_channel` protects the data in exactly the way
`export_not_net` does. **But the lane did not choose it.** A signature covers
only what was shown, the PO was shown seven names, and an engine that quietly
adds an eighth is amending a ruling on its own authority — which is the failure
this register exists to prevent.

**What it costs to answer:** one sentence from the PO. The worked case to put to
them, in plain English with a figure: *"A solar inverter reports 612 kWh of
generation. Today a utility can switch off the check that stops that 612 kWh
being filed as a customer's consumption and billed. Should they be able to?"*
## OQ-418 — `replace` and `insert & update` do the SAME thing to reads, and only one of them can be right

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-26 by the CR-038 W7 (one rail) lane, while
building the three write modes the PO asked for by name.

**Where it comes from.** PO, 2026-08-26, verbatim: *"we need insert, insert
update, repalce option in step 1 of wirzard"*. CR-038 R2 wrote the semantics
down: *"For reads the modes NEVER edit a committed row (hard rule 4): `insert`
refuses committed duplicates; `insert & update` SUPERSEDES a committed duplicate
as a correction, reason stamped; `replace` supersedes everything the file
carries."*

**The problem is in that last sentence, and it only shows up once you build it.**
*"Everything the file carries"* and *"a committed duplicate"* are **the same set
of rows** — every row in the file whose (meter, date, register) already has a
reading on file. So `replace` and `insert & update` were built identical, they
are tested identical
(`test_w7__replace_supersedes_the_same_way_as_upsert`), and the wizard says so
in the operator's own words.

**What would make them different is what `replace` does to readings that are ON
FILE and NOT IN THE FILE — and there is no lawful answer to guess at.** The
other importer's `replace` retires what is missing (BR-MET-099, PO-ruled
2026-08-21, *"it is 'replace, and retire what is missing'"*). For a meter
reading, "retire" has no meaning that survives contact with the law:

| Option | What it would do to the 60 readings on file and not in this file | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Nothing (what is built)** | leaves them exactly as they are | LAWFUL. But then two controls do one thing, which is the BR-MET-099 complaint in reverse — *"a mode called 'replace the batch' that leaves 41 rows standing is a control whose name is a lie"* |
| **B · Delete them** | removes committed `meter_reads` rows | ⛔ **FORBIDDEN.** CLAUDE.md hard rule 4 / B2 DB-6 / migration 0007's immutability trigger. Not on the table; listed so nobody re-proposes it |
| **C · Supersede them with nothing** | closes each head with `superseded_by_id` pointing at no row | ⛔ **NOT A THING.** A correction with no corrected value; `uq_meter_reads_head` and every downstream reader assume exactly one live head per key. A bill run would price a meter that has readings and no head |
| **D · Flag them** | writes a review flag ("this reading was not in the replacement file") onto each | LAWFUL, and the only option that gives `replace` a distinct, honest behaviour. ⚠ Costs a rule, a flag vocabulary and a place to work the flags from — and would mean uploading a partial file MARKS 60 innocent readings |
| **E · Drop the third mode** | offer two: `insert` and `insert & update` | LAWFUL and the smallest product. ⚠ **The PO asked for three by name**, so this needs their word, not ours |

**Worked figures, so the choice is concrete.** CY-001 holds **1,240** meters.
A clerk uploads a corrections file carrying **1,180** rows in `replace` mode.
Today: 1,180 readings are corrected and the other **60** are untouched — the
same result `insert & update` gives. Under **D**, those 60 would each gain a
review flag; under **E**, the clerk would have picked `insert & update` and the
question would never arise.

**Recommendation: E, unless the PO wants D.** Two modes that behave identically
are worse than two modes, because the operator reasonably assumes the scarier
one does something scarier. But the PO named three and only they can withdraw
one.

**What is built while this is open**, so nothing is blocked: all three modes are
offered, `replace` is RECORDED on the batch (`read_import_batches.write_mode`),
the two superseding modes behave identically, and the wizard's caution says that
in a clerk's words rather than implying a behaviour the server does not have.
Whichever way this is ruled, the recorded mode means the answer applies without
a data migration.

## OQ-419 — onboarding's "opening reads" step has a rail and no NAME

**Status:** ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-27 — "AN ORDINARY UPLOAD THAT HAPPENS TO BE
FIRST". NOTHING WAS BUILT AND NOTHING IS OWED.** PO verbatim: *"a) An ordinary
upload that happens to be first"*. None of options A–D is taken: no sixth
`event_context`, no batch-level `is_cutover` column, no naming convention, and
option D turns out to have been built all along (below).

**⚠ THIS CLOSURE WAS VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because a "nothing to do"
that is wrong is worse than a task.** Three measurements, 2026-08-27:

  1. **The five stay five.** `apps.metering.models.EVENT_CONTEXTS` is
     `("move_in", "move_out", "transfer", "disconnect", "new_connect")` and
     gains nothing. A cutover read carries `event_context = NULL`, which is
     exactly what every ordinary import and manual batch already carries — no
     branch, no default, no sixth word anywhere.
  2. **The reads rail genuinely is the target.** `import_runs.TARGETS` is
     `(premises, units, assets_meters, assets_submeters, assets_devices,
     accounts)` — six, ending at accounts — and opening reads are NOT one of
     them and should not be: they post through the S28 stage → validate →
     commit pipeline, a different rail, complete, idempotent, and already
     driven by a clerk today.
  3. ⚠ **AND THIS QUESTION'S OWN CENTRAL MEASUREMENT WAS WRONG WHEN IT WAS
     WRITTEN — which is the finding worth more than the ruling.** The text
     below says BR-CUS-047's order *"is written in exactly three places … and
     every one of them STOPS at Accounts"*. **All three name the fifth step**,
     and one of them always did:
     `apps/customers/account_import.TEMPLATE_NOTES` — *"Import order
     (BR-CUS-047): premises -> units+plans -> assets -> ACCOUNTS -> opening
     reads."* — present in the commit that created the file;
     `apps/metering/import_rules.py:786` and `apps/metering/import_runs.py:648`
     carry the same sentence. So **option D, *"the half that is unambiguously
     missing"*, was not missing.** What stops at accounts is the RUNNER's
     target tuple, which is a different fact and the correct one.
     **The lesson: a measurement quoted from a neighbouring module's prose is
     not a measurement.** The question was still worth asking — the vocabulary
     half was real and only the PO could rule it.

**Recorded in:** the CR-038 coverage row and the CR-038 open-question list
(`12-governance/11-change-requests.md`) and the decision log, so the next agent
does not re-open it.

**The original text follows, unedited**, because the reasoning that produced a
correct question from a faulty measurement is worth keeping.

**Status when raised:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-26 by the CR-038 W7 (one rail)
lane, after measuring what BR-CUS-047's last step actually lacks.

**The CR-038 coverage map lists this as *"order documented, no target"*, and
after W7 that description is out of date in a way worth writing down: THE TARGET
EXISTS.** The reads rail loads meter readings from a CSV; a cutover's opening
reads are meter readings in a CSV; a clerk can upload them today and they will
post correctly. Nothing needs building for the DATA to arrive.

**What is genuinely missing is a WORD.** BR-CUS-047's order — *"Premises →
Units+Plans → Assets → **Accounts** → opening reads"* — is written in exactly
three places (`account_import.TEMPLATE_NOTES`, `import_rules.py`,
`import_runs.py`) and every one of them STOPS at Accounts. There is no way for a
tenant, or for us, to look at a posted batch afterwards and say *these are the
readings the utility opened its books with*. Concretely, the reads that migrate
a utility's 1,240 meters on day one are indistinguishable from the reads of any
ordinary August cycle: same `source_kind`, same `read_method`, `event_context`
NULL.

**Why `event_context` is not simply the answer.** BR-MET-128 (PO 2026-08-26)
ruled that vocabulary and named its five values —
`move_in · move_out · transfer · disconnect · new_connect` — from the PO's own
sentence: *"it will be as per event - bascially we will ahve to create an record
in reading that such reading ahs been colelcted - and it is generated due to
that event"*. **A cutover is not one of those five**, and adding a sixth value to
a vocabulary the PO enumerated four hours earlier is precisely the kind of quiet
widening CLAUDE.md forbids. So no code was written and this asks instead.

| Option | What it means | Cost | Consequence |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A · A sixth `event_context`: `cutover`** | an opening read is an event read whose event is "the utility went live" | one tuple entry, one label, one migration-free change (the column exists) | ⚠ stretches BR-MET-128's own definition — the other five are things that happen to ONE customer at ONE premise; a cutover happens to the whole book. The read detail would say *"collected because of: cutover"*, which reads oddly on 1,240 rows |
| **B · A batch-level flag, not a read-level one** — `read_import_batches.is_cutover` | the BATCH is the cutover, the readings are ordinary readings | one nullable column + one stage-1 checkbox | honest about the shape (it IS a property of the upload, not of the meter), and it survives the fact that the readings themselves are unremarkable. ⚠ needs a migration and a rule |
| **C · Nothing new — use the existing tags** | tag the batch `manual`/`csv` with a `file_name` like `cutover-opening-reads.csv` | zero | ⚠ a naming convention is not a record. Nothing can query it, no screen can show it, and the next agent cannot find it |
| **D · Add the step to the onboarding checklist only** | the ORDER gets its fifth step in the three places that stop at Accounts, pointing the operator at the reads rail; nothing is stamped on the data | small, and it is the half that is unambiguously missing | closes the *"order documented, no target"* complaint without inventing a vocabulary. ⚠ leaves the posted readings unmarked, which is the other half |

**Worked case, so the choice is concrete.** Brazos Bend goes live with **1,240**
meters. The clerk imports premises, units, assets and **1,144** accounts, then
uploads **1,240** opening readings. Six months later somebody asks *"was the
April spike real, or was our opening register wrong?"*. Under **A** or **B**
that question is one filter away. Under **C** it is a guess about a file name.
Under **D** the clerk was at least told to do it.

**Recommendation: D now, and B rather than A if a mark is wanted.** D is the
half that needs no ruling — the documented order literally omits its own last
step from every list that renders it — and it can land in any lane. B fits the
shape of the thing (a cutover is a property of an upload) without stretching a
vocabulary the PO enumerated this morning.

**Nothing is blocked.** Opening reads load through the rail today, correctly and
idempotently, under whichever answer arrives; **A** and **B** are both additive
and neither invalidates a reading already posted.
## OQ-420 — a dispute is open and NOTHING RECORDS HOW MUCH IS DISPUTED: what ages while we investigate? 🔒

⚠ **RENUMBERED FROM OQ-418 BY THE MERGE LANE, 2026-08-26.** Two lanes minted
`OQ-418` the same afternoon because the integrator handed both the same
watermark — see DEF-819. `OQ-418` is CR-038 W7's question about `replace`
versus `insert & update`; this is the disputed-amount question, and the
`NotImplementedError` in `apps/billing/late_fee.ageable_portion` cites this
number, not that one.

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-26 by the BR-MET-132/133 lane, which BUILT
the arithmetic and STUBBED the case it cannot answer
(`apps/billing/late_fee.ageable_portion` → `NotImplementedError("OQ-420")`).

**This is a money question and it is a 🔒 sensitive path.** B4 is ❄️ FROZEN;
nothing below invents a figure.

**BR-MET-133 clause 4 is CONFIRMED and it is buildable — for a bill whose
disputed AMOUNT is known.** PO verbatim 2026-08-26: *"Bill stands, resolution
through the billed-correction door, and the disputed amount doesn't age into
late fees while open"*, and the rule adds *"the undisputed remainder of the
bill ages normally"*. Worked, and this arithmetic IS built and tested: Sarah's
July bill is **$184.20**; she disputes **$47.00**; **$137.20** ages and is what
BR-BIL-001's `max($5, 1.5% × overdue)` is assessed on, and **$47.00** does not.

**The gap: nothing in this repository stores a disputed amount.** Measured
2026-08-26, and it is the same measurement `apps/customers/move_out_settlement.py`
recorded on 2026-08-24 for BR-CUS-096 — no model, no column, no service writes
one. What DOES exist is `meter_reads.disputed_at` / `dispute_reason`, and that
is **a quantity in dispute, not a sum of money**: a customer saying "the meter
says 684 kWh and the property was empty" has disputed a READING, and how many
dollars of a multi-service bill that reading is responsible for is not written
anywhere. So the product can tell, exactly, WHETHER a dispute is open on a
bill, and cannot tell HOW MUCH of it is disputed.

**The question, in plain English: while a customer's dispute is open and we
cannot say how much of the bill it covers, what accrues late fees?**

| Answer | On Sarah's $184.20 bill | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Nothing ages — hold the WHOLE bill out of ageing until the dispute closes** | $0.00 ages; no late fee while it is open | ⚠ the rule says *"the undisputed remainder ages normally"*, so this over-applies it: a customer disputing $47 of $184.20 gets the other $137.20 interest-free for as long as the investigation takes, and a dispute becomes a way to stop the clock on a whole bill |
| **B · Everything ages — the exclusion applies only where an amount is recorded** | all $184.20 ages; fee assessed as though nothing were disputed | ⚠ this is the harm the ruling exists to prevent, in the ONLY case that can occur today (no amount is ever recorded), so BR-MET-133 clause 4 would ship doing nothing |
| **C · Record the disputed amount — make the clerk state it when raising a dispute on a billed reading** | the clerk types $47.00; $137.20 ages | new column + a required field on the dispute modal; and a clerk raising a dispute from a READING may not know which dollars it moved. It also asks the product to store a figure the customer asserted, next to figures the utility computed |

**Recommendation: C, with A as the interim.** C is the only answer that makes
the ruled arithmetic reachable, and A is the safe direction for the bills that
already exist with no figure on them — a customer under investigation is not
charged for our days, which is the sentence the PO actually said. B is
recorded because it is what shipping nothing would silently do.

**What is built today, so nothing is silently guessed:** the partial-exclusion
arithmetic (`ageable_portion`), its interaction with the $25.00 balance floor,
and the resolver that answers *is a dispute open on this bill* are all built and
tested. An open dispute whose amount is unreadable **raises
`NotImplementedError("OQ-420")`** rather than picking A or B — `assess_late_fee`
has no production caller yet (S31.2/US-BIL-002 is unbuilt), so the stub blocks
nothing today and refuses to become a silent default tomorrow.
## OQ-421 — should the stored monthly usage row gain an ASSET (and register) dimension?

⚠ **RENUMBERED FROM OQ-418 BY THE MERGE LANE (DEF-819).** Three lanes minted
`OQ-418` in one afternoon because I handed all four running lanes the same
watermark instead of disjoint ranges. `OQ-418` is CR-038 W7's `replace`
question and `OQ-420` is BR-MET-133's disputed-amount question; this is the
monthly-usage grain question. The lane did nothing wrong — it followed the
number it was given.

**Status:** **CLOSED 2026-08-27 → BR-MET-141.** Raised 2026-08-26 by the
CR-038 W5 tasks 6/7/8 lane building task 8's meter half.

**THE RULING, VERBATIM:** *"(b) Store it per meter too - otherwise we will ahve
to calculate it again and again"*. **Answer B**, and the reason the PO gave IS
the requirement: recomputation cost.

⚠ **THEY CHOSE THE LESS REVERSIBLE DIRECTION KNOWINGLY.** The asymmetry below —
A → B is a migration and a backfill, B → A is a dropped column with data in it
— was put to them and is the whole content of this question. It is recorded
here so a later reader does not re-raise it as an oversight.

**WHAT WAS BUILT (2026-08-27), and the two things that answer the asymmetry:**

  * `meter_read_asset_monthly_usage` (metering 0039), one head row per (tenant,
    asset, channel, period_month). The REGISTER is in the key, so DEF-798's
    measured 698 kWh is unrepresentable rather than merely absent.
  * **One derivation, never two** — the decision log's one constraint on the
    build. `monthly_usage_service._fact_rows` is now the single place a
    `meter_reads` row becomes a `ReadFact`; both grains group the same pairs
    and both hand `MonthFigure`s to one serialiser. Both are written by ONE
    `recompute_account` call in ONE transaction, so neither can be stale
    relative to the other.
  * **A CACHE, NOT A FACT.** The S50 payload reads a stored row when one exists
    and computes the identical figure when none does. Dropping the table
    returns the product to its 2026-08-26 behaviour and loses no statement
    about any customer — asserted point for point by
    `tests/test_oq_421_per_meter_monthly_usage.py::…tc3`. **That is what makes
    the reversal cheap in MEANING even though it is not cheap in SCHEMA.**

**STILL OPEN AND NOT CLOSED BY THIS:** `OQ-358` (a month whose reads for one
account and one service disagree about the unit) is untouched — a mixed-unit
month raises before anything is stored, at either grain.

**What the PO asked for**, verbatim: *"We ahve to calcualet last 12 month
consumption from these readings and display it on account and meters"*. Both
halves are now built and both are correct. They are **not** built the same way,
and the difference is a real fork the PO should settle rather than a shortcut
this lane took.

**The account half reads a STORED row.** BR-MET-106's `monthly_usage` table is
keyed `(tenant, account, service, period_month)` — the figure is computed once,
written, restated on a correction, and the S21 Usage tab reads it back.

**The meter half cannot**, because that table has no asset column and no channel
column. A meter is neither of its keys: one account can hold several meters on
one service, and one meter can hold several registers whose figures BR-MET-135
(`generation`) and BR-RAT-014 (demand, in kW) forbid adding together. So
`apps/metering/asset_usage.py` computes the meter's months from that meter's own
committed reads, through the *same* `monthly_usage` rules module the account tab
calls — same functions, not a copy — and says so on the wire (`source:
"computed_from_reads"`, plus `stored_source_absent` naming this question).

**The worked number, in plain English.** Sarah's meter M-4412 read 684 kWh in
July. The account tab prints 684 because a row says so. The meter strip prints
684 because it added July's reads a second time, at request time. Today they
agree, and a test asserts they agree on the single-meter case so a drift goes
red. What nobody has ruled is whether that is good enough.

| Answer | What it takes | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Leave it computed (today's state)** | nothing | two code paths produce one customer-facing number. They agree by test, not by construction. A meter with three years of reads recomputes on every tab open — cheap at <3,000 connections, not free |
| **B · Add `asset_id` + `channel` to `monthly_usage`** | a migration on a signed table (🔒 migration ordering), a backfill, and the writer must fan out per meter per register | ONE stored source for both surfaces, and the meter strip becomes a plain read. It also multiplies the row count by registers × meters — the table stops being three orders of magnitude smaller than `meter_reads`, which is the reason `MonthlyUsage` is deliberately unpartitioned |
| **C · Store the account row only, and mark the meter strip explicitly derived** | a sentence on screen | which is what shipped, so C is A with the honesty already paid for |

**Recommendation: A/C for now, B only if a second consumer appears.** One
computed surface reading the same rules is not the drift hazard two stored
tables would be. But this lane may not choose it: B is a schema change on a
table BR-MET-106 signed, and the prime directive says a lane implements signed
law and never invents it.

**⚠ Cheap to reverse in one direction only.** Going A → B later is a migration
plus a backfill and nothing is lost. Going B → A is a dropped column with data
in it. That asymmetry is the argument for not building B on a guess.

## OQ-422 — may a counter reading be taken against a meter on NO cycle?

⚠ **RENUMBERED FROM OQ-419 BY THE MERGE LANE (DEF-819)** — `OQ-419` is
CR-038 W7's question about naming the onboarding opening-reads step. Same
cause as OQ-421 above.

**Status:** **CLOSED 2026-08-27 → BR-MET-140.** Raised 2026-08-26 by the
CR-038 W5 tasks 6/7/8 lane building task 6 (the quick single-reading modal).

**THE RULING, VERBATIM:** *"(b) Accept and warn"*. **Answer B**, which is the
recommendation below.

⚠ **THE `→ BR-MET-139` IN THE SCOREBOARD ROW WAS A COLLISION, NOT THIS RULE'S
ID (DEF-870).** BR-MET-139 was already CR-039 wave E's seeded-premises rule.
The rule is **BR-MET-140**.

**WHAT CHANGED FROM WHAT SHIPPED:** only the warning. The reading already
posted and the absence was already SHOWN; it is now stated as a warning with a
reason a clerk can act on (`no_route` / `route_has_no_cycle`) and the action
that fixes it, so **somebody fixes the route**. It is amber and not red,
because nothing is wrong with the reading — the configuration fault is ours.

**A's REAL GAP IS NOT CLOSED BY THIS AND THE RULE SAYS SO:** an untagged read
is still invisible to W1's expected-vs-received completeness in every period.
The warning is the only thing that gets it chased.

**The case, worked.** A clerk at the counter has meter M-5002 in front of them
and a reading of 1,300 kWh taken today. The meter resolves to no route, or to a
route on no cycle — a new connection not yet on a walk, or a meter whose route
membership moved. **The reading is real and the customer is standing there.**

**Why this is not already answered by an existing rule.** Three point in
different directions and none of them is about this case:

  * **BR-MET-129** says a collected reading is STORED — *"if reading are
    colelcted we have to store the reading, we can give the warning, but we
    cannot reject the reading"*. That is about VEE warnings at post, not about a
    missing cycle tag.
  * **BR-MET-014** tags every batch with month/cycle/route/service and inherits
    those to every row. It assumes the cycle exists.
  * **BR-MET-122** makes an OFF-cycle meter (in the wrong cycle) a warning with
    a reason. A meter in NO cycle is a different shape: there is nothing to be
    off.

**What shipped, and it decides nothing.** `GET /reads/quick-context` answers
`cycle: null` with a reason (`no_route` or `route_has_no_cycle`), the modal
SHOWS that absence instead of offering a blank box, and the one-row batch is
staged with **no `cycle_id` field at all** rather than an empty one — because an
empty tag is a claim and absence is not.

| Answer | What it means | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Accept it, untagged** (today's behaviour) | the reading exists and is billable when the meter joins a cycle | the read has no cycle stamp, so W1's expected-vs-received completeness cannot see it in any period. It is a real reading that is invisible to the chase list |
| **B · Accept it and WARN, like BR-MET-122** | same, plus a flag a person works from S25 | needs a rule row and a flag name; it is the shape BR-MET-122 already established, one case over |
| **C · Refuse until the meter is on a cycle** | the clerk fixes the setup first | it turns a customer standing at the counter away over a configuration fault that is ours, which is the posture BR-MET-129 explicitly rejects for collected readings |

**Recommendation: B.** It keeps BR-MET-129's promise (the reading is never
rejected) and closes A's real gap (an untagged read nobody can chase) with the
mechanism the PO has already approved once for the neighbouring case.

**⚠ NOT CHOSEN HERE.** A is what shipped because it is the smallest honest
behaviour, and the modal states the absence on screen so nothing is hidden from
the clerk. B needs a rule row and a flag the PO signs.

    **NEW** number rather than reusing the closed case's — BR-TEN-035 never
    reuses, and a reopened case is a new document.
  * **Cases opened before today keep a NULL number.** No backfill: the question
    asked for one in the same breath and the ruling did not grant one, and the
    `numbering_series_missing` reason is already served beside every such row.
    ⚠ **A tenant provisioned before today has no `disconnect_case` row either**
    — `_seed_number_series` is `get_or_create`, so the repair door is
    `manage.py seed_demo --tenant <subdomain>`, exactly as for `transfer`.

⚠ **THE `DSP-` COLLISION IS ACCEPTED, NOT SOLVED.** The dispatch batch opens
`DSP-{YY}{MM}{DD}-{00}` and sits one character away in a list an admin reads
down. It was raised in this question, the choice does not fix it, and it is
named here and in `core/numbering.py` so the next person to see them adjacent
knows it was seen. It raises no CR-005 duplicate-prefix warning — the literals
`DSC-` and `DSP-` differ — and a test pins both.

**The record of the refusal that made this cheap**, kept for the same reason
OQ-426's is: the wave D lane BUILT the column and the in-transaction allocation
and **refused to pick the prefix**, so closing this was one catalogue row, five
test pins, one label and no schema change.

**The original question follows, unedited.**

**Where this comes from.** CR-039 Wave D task 16, verbatim: *"the same for
disconnect"*, against the same finding 5 above.

**What the design draws — nothing, and this one has a competing precedent.**

  * `18-cr030-onboarding-design.md` §5.8.2, the list's columns, verbatim:
    *"`ACCOUNT` · `CUSTOMER` · `ADDRESS` · `OWED` · `TIER` · `CUT DATE` · `LAST
    NOTICE` · `STATE`"*. **No reference column.**
  * §5.8.6's nine seeded rows carry `A-11507`, `A-11488`, `A-11340`, `A-11720`,
    `A-11812`, `A-11780`, `A-11902`, `A-11655`, `A-11933` — **account numbers,
    and no case id.**
  * §5.8.7's wizard as drawn (`DSC-02.1` … `DSC-02.5`) shows no case reference
    on any of the five steps. ⚠ `DSC-01` / `DSC-02.n` are SHOT NAMES again.
  * ⚠ **AND r10 DRAWS A DISCONNECT AS A WORK ORDER.** The clickable reference
    contains, verbatim: *"Disconnect work order raised · `WO-4833`"*, plus
    `'Disconnect · non-pay', premise:'1408 Elm St · A-10432'` in its work-order
    rows and *"Disconnect — non-payment · 5 steps"*. **The one number r10 ever
    puts on a disconnection is a `WO-` number**, and `work_order` is a seeded
    series in the catalogue today (`WO-{0000}`, GROUP_WORK) with **no live
    caller**.

**So this question is genuinely different from OQ-426**, and it must not be
answered by symmetry with it: **is a disconnect case its own document, or is it
the work order r10 already draws?** They are not the same answer. A case can sit
on the ladder for months across three notices and a hold; a work order is the
visit that turns the water off. `disconnect_cases` and `work_orders` would also
be one counter under option C, and OQ-249 (is Work a tenth module?) is open.

**The question, in plain English: when a customer rings about the disconnection
notice they were sent, what does the clerk read back?**

| Answer | What the first case on a new tenant is called | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · `DSC-{YY}-{0000}`** | **`DSC-26-0001`** | the case is its own document with its own counter; matches OQ-426 option A. `DSC-` collides with no seeded prefix — ⚠ but `DSP-` (dispatch batch) is one character away in a list an admin reads down |
| **B · `DC-{YY}-{0000}`** | **`DC-26-0001`** | shorter to read down a phone; ⚠ `DC` is not a word and means nothing to a customer holding the notice |
| **C · the WORK ORDER series** | **`WO-4833`**-shaped | **what r10 actually draws.** No new series, no new prefix, nothing invented. ⚠ it makes a months-long collections case and a two-hour field visit the same kind of thing, and OQ-249 has not said whether work orders are in this product |
| **D · a bare counter, `{00000}`** | **`00001`** | as OQ-426 D |

**Recommendation: NONE — this one needs the PO, not a lane's preference.** C has
prototype evidence behind it and A has consistency, and the choice between them
is a product judgment about what a disconnect case IS. That is the same shape as
tasks 17–19 (*"decide what a move-in and move-out ARE"*), which are blocked for
exactly this reason.

**⚠ NOT CHOSEN. Nothing below picks one.** `disconnect_cases.case_no` exists,
`open_case` and the post-closure restart allocate from the series by name inside
their creating transaction, the allocation reports `numbering_series_missing`
while no catalogue row exists, and S90 renders the absence with its reason.
**The same four hand-pinned places listed at the foot of OQ-426 are owed when
this closes**, and the same backfill question applies to cases opened before it.

## OQ-423 — a premises' jurisdiction is corrected. Does that reach bills already issued? 🔒

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-27 by the CR-039 wave C tasks 10/11 lane,
building *"a way to SET jurisdiction"*. **Reserved range DEF-825–829 /
OQ-423–425 (DEF-819's collision fix); these IDs are not taken from a watermark. The range read
DEF-824–829 until 2026-08-27, when the coordinator spent 824 itself and told
this lane to move — the row that had it is now DEF-826.**

**Why it is asked NOW and could not be asked before.** Until this lane,
`premises.inside_city_limits` had no writer at any layer (`DEF-517`) — so
nobody could change it and the question could not arise. From 2026-08-27 a
clerk can change it on the PRM-01 edit modal and on the S16 guided add, and
BR-RAT-102 makes that change worth money.

**The case, worked, on the seeded estate.** `161 Silver Creek Rd` is on the
sample Residential plan, which states r10's outside-city factor of **1.5**. In
June 2026 the address used **18 kgal**:

| | inside the city | outside the city |
|---|---|---|
| water usage (`[W] §1` ladder) | $109.00 | **$163.50** |
| water base | $8.00 | **$12.00** |
| **the difference on ONE bill** | | **$58.50** |

So a clerk who ticks *Outside city limits* on an address that was recorded
*Inside* has just said that this customer's last bill was $58.50 short — or, the
other way round, $58.50 too much. **Nothing in the repo says what happens to
that bill.**

**What the product does today, and it is a stated assumption rather than a
ruling.** `metering.services.update_premises` writes the column and stops.
Every issued invoice, invoice line, payment and journal entry is untouched; the
NEXT bill run reads the new value and prices accordingly. That follows
CLAUDE.md hard rule 4 — *no UPDATE/DELETE on issued invoices; corrections are
new rows* — and it is the only behaviour available without inventing an
adjustment nobody signed. It is written into `update_premises`'s docstring and
pinned by `tests/test_cr039_c10_premises_jurisdiction_write.py::
test_cr039_c10__oq423_changing_the_flag_touches_no_issued_invoice`.

**What is genuinely undecided:**

| Answer | What it means | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Forward only** (today's behaviour) | the correction affects the next bill and nothing else | a customer under-charged for six months keeps the money, and a customer over-charged never gets it back unless a human notices and raises a credit by hand |
| **B · Forward, plus a prompt** | the screen says *"3 issued bills were priced at the old jurisdiction"* and offers to open the adjustment screen | needs a rule for how far back to look, and a person still decides |
| **C · Automatic back-adjustment** | the product raises correcting lines itself | it needs a signed rule for the window, the effective date, and who authorises it — and it writes money on a screen the clerk thought was an address edit |

**A second half of the same question, and it is one step earlier:** a bill run
is OPEN with DRAFT bills already calculated when the flag changes. A draft is
not immutable, so hard rule 4 does not answer it. Today nothing re-calculates.

**⚠ NOT CHOSEN HERE.** A is what shipped, because it is the only one of the
three that writes no money on an unsigned rule.

## OQ-424 — the outside-city multiplier and the percent-of-water sewer charge: does it flow through? 🔒

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-27 by the CR-039 wave C tasks 10/11 lane, on
the first bill in this product's history where both of these rules were live at
once.

**Two signed statements that have never met before, and on Silver Creek they
now do.**

* **Design §A4 S2**, verbatim: *"BASE-S $8.00 (flat everywhere — the multiplier
  does NOT touch sewer)"*, and r10 in four words: *"sewer is flat everywhere"*.
  §A4's estate prices sewer as a **BASE**.
* **BR-RAT-015** ❄️ FROZEN: sewer is **40% of the WATER USAGE CHARGE**. Silver
  Creek's sewer has a base of **$0.00** and is priced entirely this way.

So the exemption §A4 states reaches a line that is zero, and the sewer charge
that actually bills is derived from a water usage charge the multiplier HAS
already moved.

**Worked, on `161 Silver Creek Rd`, June 2026, 18 kgal:**

| | inside the city | outside the city |
|---|---|---|
| water usage | $109.00 | $163.50 |
| sewer at 40% of it | $43.60 | **$65.40** |

**$21.80 a month on one address**, from a rule that says sewer is flat
everywhere and a rule that says sewer follows water.

**Why this is a question and not a defect.** Neither rule is wrong and neither
is being broken. `sewer` IS on the plan's exempt list, R5 DOES hand it a factor
of 1, and its own base does not move. The rise is composition: 40% of a bigger
number. Both readings are defensible —

| Answer | What it means | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · It flows through** (today's behaviour) | the percentage is taken of what water actually billed | *"sewer is flat everywhere"* is false on any estate that prices sewer as a percentage, and the sentence stays in the design saying otherwise |
| **B · It does not** | the percentage is taken of the INSIDE-city water charge, and sewer is genuinely flat | it needs a new rule saying which water figure the percentage reads, and it touches `percent_of_service` — B4/B5 adjacent, so a re-sign via HUMAN-GUIDE §6 |

**⚠ NOT CHOSEN HERE, AND NOT STUBBED EITHER.** No new code produces this
behaviour — it is what two already-signed rules compose to, and a
`NotImplementedError` here would refuse a bill in order to ask a question. The
figure is asserted in `tests/test_cr039_c11_seeded_surcharge.py` so the day the
PO rules B, that test is what goes red and names the place to build it.

## OQ-500 — when a premises has a TYPED owner, is that owner the default payer? 🔒

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-27 by the CR-039 wave C tasks 12–14 lane, the
moment a premises could name a party in two places at once.

**This is a money question and it is live today.** `apps/customers/services.py`
opens an account with no contact by falling back to the premises' free text,
and its own comment quotes the PO: *"payer = the premises' owner/manager"* (PO
2026-08-22). It reads `premises.owner_manager` — the string — and copies it into
`contact.full_name`.

**After CR-039 wave C task 12 a premises can hold BOTH:** the free-text
`owner_manager` *"Mill Pond Apartments LP"* and an owner ROW that is the same
party, typed `landlord`, carrying an email, a phone and a link to the customer
record they already are.

**What this lane did: nothing.** `open_account` is untouched, still reads the
string, still refuses when there is none. Changing which of the two it reads
changes who a new account bills and what contact details that bill carries — on
a screen a clerk opened to add an address.

| Answer | What it means | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · The string, always** (today's behaviour) | the typed record is documentation and the money path ignores it | the product keeps routing money at a name it cannot resolve, which is CR-039 finding 4 left open after the wave that was supposed to close it |
| **B · The typed owner when there is one, the string otherwise** | the payer becomes a resolvable party with contact details; the string is the fallback for an unmatched premises | one behaviour, two sources, for as long as BR-MET-151's matching backlog exists — and a premises matched *after* an account opened does not retro-change that account's payer |
| **C · The typed owner, and refuse when there is none** | one source of truth | it BLOCKS account creation on every unmatched premises, which is every premises on every existing tenant on the day this ships |

**⚠ NOT CHOSEN HERE, AND NOT STUBBED.** A `NotImplementedError` would refuse to
open an account in order to ask a question; A is what the code already does and
it is written down rather than left as an absence. The day the PO rules B or C,
`tests/test_cr039_c12_premises_owner.py::test_oq_500__open_account_still_reads_
the_free_text` is what goes red and names the place to build it.

## OQ-501 — once a tenant is fully matched, is `premises.owner_manager` retired?

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-27 by the CR-039 wave C tasks 12–14 lane.

BR-MET-151 keeps the free-text column: it is the provenance of a match, it is
what an unmatched premises still has, and it is what `open_account` reads
(`OQ-500`). So a matched premises carries the name **twice** — once as text,
once as a typed row — and the two can drift the moment somebody edits one.

| Answer | What it means | The cost |
|---|---|---|
| **A · Keep both for ever** (today) | the string is legacy provenance and the row is the truth | two writable copies of one fact, and the S14 search column reads the string |
| **B · Read-only once matched** | the box greys out when an owner is linked | needs a rule for un-matching, and the CSV importer offers the column |
| **C · Drop the column once every tenant is matched** | one fact, one place | it is a destructive migration on a column `open_account` reads, so it cannot precede `OQ-500`, and *"every tenant is matched"* is a condition no deployment can assert about a customer's database |

**⚠ NOT CHOSEN HERE.** A is what shipped. This question is ordered AFTER
`OQ-500`: which column the money path reads has to be settled before either
column can be taken away.

## OQ-502 — are the five owner categories the complete list, or may a tenant add its own?

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-27 by the CR-039 wave C tasks 12–14 lane.

The PO ruled *"category is okay, no richer text"* over the five —
owner-occupier · landlord · property manager · HOA · builder. **Nothing was put
to them about whether a tenant may add a sixth**, and the decision log records
the gap in those words: *"Every other reference vocabulary in this product is
tenant-extensible (BR-TEN-036) and nothing was put to the PO about this one, so
the build follows the house pattern and the row says so."*

**What shipped: the house pattern.** `owner_categories` is a normal S8
reference list — seeded with the five as `is_system`, and a tenant may add
`executor_of_estate`, `trust` or `receiver` exactly as it may add an area or a
meter size class (DB-14, BR-TEN-036, BR-TEN-150).

**Why this is a question rather than a decision.** A CLOSED list is a real
alternative with a real consequence: a fixed five means every tenant's owner
data is comparable, and a platform report could count landlords across
customers. An extensible list makes that report meaningless and makes the
vocabulary the tenant's own. Both are defensible; only one was chosen, by
default, by an existing rule rather than by the PO.

**⚠ NOT STUBBED.** BR-TEN-036 is a signed rule and following it is not a guess.
If the PO closes the list, the change is one flag on the handler and a test.

## OQ-503 — must a premises owner be reachable?

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-27 by the CR-039 wave C tasks 12–14 lane.

The ruling names **contact details** as part of the typed record and gives the
reason in the same sentence: *"so there is a way to reach whoever is named when
a unit is vacant or a bill bounces"*. It does not say whether a record with no
email and no phone may be saved.

**What shipped:** all three contact columns are optional. A `builder` holding a
site before handover may be a name and a category and nothing else, and refusing
to record that party at all would be worse than recording them without a phone
number.

**The unresolved half is the one the ruling's own reason names.** Three of the
five occupancy states bill the OWNER. An owner who is the payer and carries no
email and no phone is precisely the *"bill bounces and there is no way to reach
them"* case the contact details were asked for. Whether the category that PAYS
must carry at least one contact method is the question.

**⚠ NOT CHOSEN HERE, AND NOT STUBBED** — a required field invented here would
refuse to save an owner nobody said was unsaveable.

## OQ-600 — does a list's search prompt start with the verb, or name the fields bare?

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-27 by the CR-041 tasks 2–6 lane. **Copy only.
No rule, no money, no data.** Every list has a prompt now; this asks which of two
sentence shapes all of them should use.

**B14 rule 19, verbatim:** *"Search placeholders read `Search {entities}…` per
module."* Twenty-three searchable lists carry a prompt as of today, and **eighteen
follow that grammar while five do not**:

| Shape | Lists | Example |
|---|---|---|
| **`Search …`** — rule 19's own grammar | 18 | *"Search bill #, account # or customer…"* · *"Search meter #…"* · *"Search plan name or code…"* |
| **Bare field list, no verb** | 5 | *"Customer, account #, address, or meter #…"* (Disconnects · Move-ins · Move-outs · New connects · Transfers) |

**Why the five are the way they are, because it is not carelessness.** Each of
those sentences is **B18's own text**, and the server serves the identical string
as `search.hint` — `disconnect_reads.SEARCH_HINT`, `MOVE_IN_SEARCH_HINT`,
`MOVE_OUT_SEARCH_HINT`, `transfer_reads.SEARCH_HINT`, and
`connection_reads._search`'s docstring. Rewriting the copy would put the drawn
prompt and the served hint into disagreement about one box, which is the exact
class of drift CR-041 exists to remove. So this lane **wired them unchanged and
raised the question** rather than choosing.

**The two answers, and each has a real cost.**

* **A · Everything takes rule 19's `Search …`.** One grammar in twenty-three
  toolbars. Costs: five sentences change in eleven catalogues (55 values), and
  the five server `SEARCH_HINT` constants must change in the same commit or the
  hint and the prompt disagree — which also touches B18's quoted text.
* **B · Amend rule 19 to allow the bare form where the server publishes the
  hint.** Costs nothing today and makes the rule describe the product. Risk: the
  next author has to know which of two grammars applies, and a rule with a
  carve-out is a rule people get wrong.

**⚠ NOT CHOSEN HERE.** Rule 19 is ratified law and the five sentences are a
signed design document's own words; picking between them is a PO copy call, and
the difference is visible on five screens a clerk uses daily. **Nothing is
blocked** — all twenty-three prompts are live either way, and whichever answer
comes back is a copy edit, not a rebuild.

**⚠ NOT STUBBED, deliberately.** There is nothing to refuse: both shapes render,
both are true, and a `NotImplementedError` over a placeholder would take a
working box off five screens to make a point about punctuation.

## OQ-590 — where does a PARKED BILLING RUN live, and what is it called?

> ✅ **CLOSED 2026-08-27 — OPTION B, A REAL PARKED QUEUE.** PO verbatim: *"B — a Parked
> section on the Billing list — Real queue, real work"*. ⚠ **The PO OVERRULED the
> lane's recommendation, and the reason is worth keeping:** the lane recommended (A),
> the save-and-exit link, on the grounds that a billing run is usually finished in one
> sitting. A parked run now gets its own section on the Billing list, so it is findable
> by someone who did not park it. This closes `DEF-1043`'s open half and gives
> `WizardParkFlow` its sixth flow — which the CR-043 wizard lane refused to invent
> precisely because no surface existed to invent it against.

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-27 by the CR-043 Run bills lane, on the PO's
second report of the same gap: *"why two button at botton , I can not save and
exit"*. Blocks **DEF-1043**; does NOT block **Save & exit**, which is wired and
shipped in the same commit.

**What is already ruled and is not in question.** `BR-SHL-047` (PO 2026-08-24,
verbatim *"Park it"*) says **every wizard parks**. Six wizards mount
`WizardFrame`. This is the sixth.

**What the ruling does not reach, and why it cannot be answered here.** Park is
not a control, it is a stored row with a home:

| The thing | What exists | What a bill run has |
|---|---|---|
| `WizardParkFlow` | a CLOSED, server-enforced vocabulary of **five** — `move_in`, `move_out`, `transfer`, `disconnect`, `new_connect` | **no value.** Sending a sixth is a 400 |
| `PARKED_HOME_PATHS` | each flow → the accounts tab its parked drafts appear on | **no tab.** CR-035 AMENDMENT 1 put parked drafts *"directly on each request"* — PO verbatim, *"seperate queue not reequired"* — and there is no Run bills queue |
| `subject_ref` | a JSON copy of the ids the draft describes, with **no FK** (BR-SHL-048 (a)) | a cycle + a period, which is fine — this half is not the problem |

**So the two questions, in plain English, with the concrete case:**

1. *A clerk fills in the July run for cycle 06-A, gets as far as reviewing the
   customers, and has to stop and phone somebody. Where should that half-done
   run be waiting for them tomorrow morning?* A "Parked runs" section on the
   Billing list is the obvious answer and it is a NEW surface, which is why it
   is a question rather than a choice.
2. *Is a half-filled run even the right thing to park, given the run itself
   already exists on the server the moment step 1 is passed and can be reopened
   from its own link?* If the answer is that the LINK is the park, then
   BR-SHL-047 is already satisfied here by Save & exit and this question closes
   with no build at all — which is the outcome worth checking first, because it
   is free.

**⚠ NOTHING IS ASSUMED AND NOTHING IS STUBBED.** The control renders DISABLED
carrying its reason (BR-SHL-025) — *"A billing run cannot be parked yet:
nothing would list it. Use Save & exit — this link reopens exactly here."* —
which is a true sentence a clerk can act on today. Inventing a sixth flow value
would be this lane widening a server-enforced vocabulary nobody asked to widen.

## OQ-680 — which conditions must BLOCK a transfer or a disconnect, and which merely warn?

**Status:** ✅ **CLOSED 2026-09-25 — NONE OF THEM BLOCK. THE PRODUCT WARNS AND
THE CLERK PROCEEDS.** PO ruling, verbatim: *"so please show the warining - but
dont stop clark from doing his work; we have to tell there is an issue but we
ant stop them"*. Raised 2026-08-27 by the customers high-severity lane from
**DEF-744**; open 29 days.

⚠ **THIS BODY IS REWRITTEN, NOT LEFT UNDER A CHANGED STATUS.** A body that goes
on describing the open world while its status says CLOSED is what misled three
lanes in one evening (`DEF-WRK-4030`), and the body is what a lane actually
reads. Everything below describes the world after the ruling; the question as it
was asked is kept at the end, marked as history.

### WHAT THE PRODUCT MUST DO

A condition in force — **a medical certificate, a weather moratorium, an active
payment plan, an open dispute, an unbilled cycle** — is **SHOWN** to the clerk
as a warning and **never refuses the act**. There is no override to grant,
because there is nothing to override.

⚠ **AND THE CLERK IS ASKED FOR NOTHING BEFORE PROCEEDING.** A middle path —
*proceed, but type a reason first* — was put to the PO and **declined**.
*"we ant stop them"* rules out anything a clerk must supply. No typed reason, no
tick-to-acknowledge (which is a refusal with an extra click — the PO's own
reasoning on `OQ-CUS-12515`), no supervisor.

### THE CONSEQUENCE — CAPTURED AUTOMATICALLY, NOT ASKED FOR

**If nothing blocks, the record of the override is the only protection that
exists** — for the customer and for the utility. The product captures, without
asking the clerk for anything: **which protections were in force** (by kind,
with their dates), **that the clerk was shown the warning**, **who proceeded**,
and **when**. That is not a second ruling; it is the minimum that makes *"warn
but do not stop"* defensible six months later at a hearing.

⚠ **AND NONE OF THAT IS EXPLAINED ON SCREEN.** B14 rule 33 puts RATIONALE at
zero words. The warning states the fact and its dates; it says nothing about
being recorded and nothing about why the product permits the act.

### WHAT WAS SHOWN BEFORE THE RULING, BECAUSE A SIGNATURE COVERS ONLY THAT

The PO was told in plain English that in much of North America **a medical
certificate or a weather moratorium is LAW, not process**, and that a recorded
protection is a different kind of fact from a ticked checklist. **They ruled
against blocking over that concern.** Options offered: (A) refuse — declined;
**(B) warn and allow — CHOSEN**; (C) override with a typed reason — declined.

**Why this closes all three of the original candidates and not only the one
argued.** The case for blocking is **strongest** where the condition is a legal
bar — a doctor's certificate, a regulator's cold-weather window. That is the
case that was shown, and it was declined. An active payment plan, an open
dispute and an unbilled cycle are each a *weaker* case for blocking than a legal
moratorium, and the PO's sentence is unqualified about the clerk. So the answer
to *"which block"* is **none**, and to *"which warn"* is **all**.

### WHAT THIS DOES NOT DECIDE, NAMED SO NOBODY ASSUMES IT DID

* **The unattended ladder is untouched.** `disconnects.HALT_PROTECTED` freezing
  the automatic dunning ladder — reminders, notices, the certified final letter
  — is a machine declining to act, not a clerk being stopped, and the ruling is
  about a person. **It stands as signed** and moves only on its own ruling.
* **The disconnect wizard's four-step redesign is unapproved and unstarted.**
  Nothing here says what step 1 shows or builds a protections table.
* **The words of each warning** are the building lane's, under B14 rule 33.

### WHAT IS STILL OPEN AGAINST THIS CLOSURE — THE FAN-OUT, NOT YET WALKED

This row is closed; the surfaces that cite it as OPEN are **not** amended,
because each is prose served to a clerk's screen and belongs to the lane that
owns that copy. Every one is now false and must be corrected:

| Surface | What it still says |
|---|---|
| `06-backend/apps/customers/close_out.py` `CLOSE_OUT_STATED_ABSENCES` (`close_out_clearance_not_performed`, `tracks: OQ-680`) | that the block-or-warn question *"was never put to the Product Owner (OQ-680, OPEN)"* |
| `06-backend/tests/test_def724_close_out.py` | asserts that stated absence, so it pins the OPEN world |
| Transfer + Disconnect wizard step 1, `data-tracks="OQ-680"` | states a clearance is not performed while the question is open |
| `07-frontend` disconnect wizard | ***"Recording one stops the cut. The money is still owed."*** — now FALSE (lane DSCOPY) |
| `04-docs/05-modules/03-customers/conformance/CR-094-laneG-standalone-move-out-and-transfer.md` | cites `OQ-680` as a live question |
| `12-governance/10-defect-log.csv` **DEF-744** | still open, blocked on this ruling — it is now unblocked |

⚠ **`OQ-680` HAS A SECTION AND NO TABLE ROW** (`DEF-2820` measured it among
eight such), so `common.oq_status_by_id()` cannot see this status. Closing it
here does not make any gate read it.

---

### THE QUESTION AS IT WAS ASKED — HISTORY. DO NOT BUILD FROM IT.

**How this surfaced, and it is the interesting part.** Step 1 of the Transfer and
Disconnect wizards used to carry a sentence saying no endpoint served a clearance
check. While it read as engineering prose nobody asked what the sentence was
standing in for. **Rewriting it into plain English is what made the gap visible**
— because a clerk who reads *"nothing here blocks this transfer"* reasonably
concludes that nothing blocks it. DEF-744's own words: *"the copy was doing the
work of a check."*

**What existed at the time:** neither wizard made a clearance call, and no
backend endpoint served one. Step 1 confirmed the account and moved on.

**The three candidate conditions, each already stored, each with a real reading
both ways:**

| Condition | Argument for BLOCK | Argument for WARN |
|---|---|---|
| **An active payment plan** | The instalments are an agreement about a debt on THIS account. Closing it mid-plan orphans the schedule, and BR-CUS-082 already restarts the ladder on a debt that survives closure | A household that is moving still owes the money and the plan can follow them — refusing traps a customer who is genuinely leaving |
| **An open dispute** | BR-CUS-096 already holds excess money while a dispute is open. Closing decides the money the dispute is about | A dispute over $40 should not strand a whole move-out |
| **An unbilled cycle** | The final bill cannot be right until the cycle is billed; BR-BIL-004 already refuses a move-out BEHIND an issued bill | The move-out DATE is what matters and billing catches up — this is a sequencing warning, not a bar |

**⚠ AND THE SHAPE OF THE ANSWER MATTERS AS MUCH AS THE ANSWER.** If any of the
three BLOCKED, it would need a refusal with a message key in eleven catalogues,
and a clerk would need a documented way past it — otherwise the product has a
dead end, which is the exact failure DEF-724 records one flow over. **The ruling
removes that problem rather than solving it: nothing refuses, so nothing needs a
way past.**

## OQ-681 — is `CC-RECON` a catalogue code the platform seeds, or a tenant setting? And is `DISC` the same code as B18's `CC-DISC`?

**Status:** OPEN — raised 2026-08-27 by the customers high-severity lane, from
**DEF-700**. **Blocks DEF-700's durable half.** Reference data, not money: the
reconnection fee's AMOUNT is already ruled at **$75.00** (BR-CUS-104, PO
2026-08-25, worked as `A-11340` owing $8,240.00 + $75.00 = **$8,315.00**), so
nothing here asks the PO to price anything.

**The measured facts, on this tree today:**

* `disconnects.py` looks up three codes by name — `CC-RECON`, `CC-DISC`,
  `CC-FIELD` — because `DSC-02.4` says the fee comes *"from your charge codes,
  never typed"* and BR-BIL-007 forbids a hardcoded figure.
* The demo seed writes four codes: `CONN`, **`DISC`**, `NSF`, `TAMPER`.
* So `commit_cut` resolves **no** reconnection code on **any** tenant in this
  tree, and every cut refuses — a feature unreachable the day it shipped.
* And B18's `CC-DISC` is the seed's `DISC` **under a different name**, which is
  the part a lane must not settle by picking a spelling.

**The two questions, in plain English:**

1. *When a utility signs up, should SMARTBillHub create a "Reconnection fee"
   charge code for them automatically — the way it already creates Connection
   fee, Disconnect fee, NSF fee and Tamper fee?* If yes, the code is `CC-RECON`
   at $75.00 and the feature works on every tenant from day one.
2. *The disconnect fee already exists under the code `DISC`, and the disconnect
   screen looks for `CC-DISC`. Are those the same fee?* If they are, one of the
   two names has to give — and **renaming a seeded code is a data change on
   every tenant that already has one**, which is why it is a ruling and not a
   tidy-up.

**⚠ WHY A LANE MAY NOT DECIDE (2).** Re-pointing an existing tenant's charge code
changes what a bill line is called on documents already sent. That is BR-CUS-094's
own posture about `government` in a different vocabulary: *"every existing record
keeps its code"*, and re-pointing is a human act per record.

**⚠ NOT STUBBED.** `commit_cut` already refuses by name with
`reconnect_charge_code_not_seeded` and states what is missing — the
`notifications/notices.py` posture for the same figure in the same letter,
*"Configure the reconnect charge code, then generate."* That refusal is correct
and stays until this is answered.
