## OQ-INT-12404 — which kinds of message does Postmark's `outbound` stream carry, when we have five kinds and the specification names four? (`CR-115-BRC05`, 2026-09-17)

**Status:** **OPEN.** Nothing is guessed and no second taxonomy was invented.
The MECHANISM is built and the MAPPING is this question.

### What is already true, so the question is as small as possible

A connector setting can now vary by the kind of message:
`registry.Field.per_class` maps a notification class to a value with a required
default, refused at load if a class is not one this product has. It is general —
*this setting varies by the kind of message* — and it is not a Postmark feature.

**This product's kinds of message are FIVE**, and they are notifications' own
list, not integrations': `apps/notifications/catalogs.py` `CR_CATEGORIES` —
**Billing · Collections · Payments · Service & field · Account lifecycle** —
which is `CR-007`'s own list in the PO's own order, the same five headings the
Templates library and the SET-09 filter chips use.

### The question

Postmark has **Message Streams**: `outbound` for transactional mail and
`broadcast` for bulk. The stream is chosen per message, and the specification we
were handed chooses it by four names that are **not the five we have**:

| the specification says | what this product has | fits? |
|---|---|---|
| Security — login codes, password resets | *nothing* | **no** |
| Financial — bills, receipts | **Billing** and **Payments**, two of the five | partly |
| Operational — outage alerts to everybody | **Service & field** | yes |
| Internal — staff alerts | *nothing on this axis* | **no** |

**Two of the four have no home at all.** There is no security or identity
category and no template class for a login code or a password reset — the portal's
one-time code is identity's and does not travel through the notifications
catalogue. *Internal* exists on the OTHER axis (`rule_catalog.CATEGORIES` has
`staff_system`), which is what SCHEDULES a message rather than what a message IS,
and a message in flight does not carry the rule that scheduled it — so a sender
could not resolve it.

**And the five leave one class unspoken for:** nothing in the specification says
which stream **Collections** goes on. A past-due notice is transactional to one
reading and a campaign to another, and getting it wrong is a deliverability
consequence rather than a cosmetic one.

### Options

**(a)** Map onto the five we have, and rule Collections explicitly —
e.g. Billing · Payments · Collections · Account lifecycle → `outbound`,
Service & field → `broadcast`. Security and Internal simply do not arise,
because no message of either kind goes out through this catalogue today.

**(b)** Mint a **sixth** template category, *Security*, and route identity's
one-time codes and password resets through the notifications catalogue so they
have a class at all. Bigger: it is a new category on the Templates library, the
SET-09 chips and every screen that groups by them.

**(c)** Treat the specification's four names as the vendor's own vocabulary and
keep a translation table between it and ours. Rejected in the writing of this
row: a second taxonomy is exactly what `CLAUDE.md` law 1 warns about, and it
would drift the first time either side gained a heading.

### What is built while this is open

**The mechanism, and no mapping.** No manifest declares a `per_class` value,
nothing reads one, and `Field.per_class` says so in its own docstring rather than
claiming a reader it does not have (`DEF-INT-5595` is what that costs). A
manifest naming `security` is refused at load, by name, with the list of what
exists — so the day somebody writes the Postmark manifest from the specification,
the product refuses to start and names this question instead of storing a setting
no sender could ever select.

## OQ-CUS-12407 — who may retire an account type from new business, and may a utility do it to a code it invented? (PO ruling 2026-09-17, `BR-CUS-1079`)

**Status:** ✅ **CLOSED 2026-09-18 — OPTION (a).** PO verbatim: *"go with option
a"*. **ANY TENANT ADMIN MAY SET OR CLEAR `legacy` ON ANY ROW, SEEDED ROWS
INCLUDED.** The worked case put with it: a utility stops offering `Marina berth`
on new accounts and goes on billing the eleven boats that already have it —
under `active=false` those eleven vanish from filters and reports, under
`legacy=true` they bill and report exactly as before.

⚠ **THE BODY BELOW DESCRIBES THE OPEN WORLD AND IS STALE FROM HERE DOWN — READ
THIS PARAGRAPH, NOT IT.** The card no longer serves `legacy` read-only; it is
writable. Option (b)'s objection — that a clerk clearing `government`'s flag
would undo a signed decision — was PUT to the PO and OVERRULED, so it is a
stated cost and not an oversight. `BR-CUS-094`'s ruling about what `government`
MEANS is untouched. This does NOT answer `OQ-CUS-12356` (may a category be
CHANGED after an account is opened), which stays **OPEN**, nor `DEF-CUS-5135`'s
hole where `account_subtype` is patchable and never validated against the
account's type. Recorded in `12-governance/02-decision-log.md`, 2026-09-18.

### What is already true, so the question is as small as possible

`account_types` carries **three** axes and they are not synonyms:

* `active = false` — the code is retired from **every** surface.
* `legacy = true` — the code is **unselectable on new records and lawful
  everywhere else**: still a valid FK, still filterable, still priceable, every
  existing account keeps it and bills exactly as it did (`BR-CUS-094`).
* `is_system` — seeded, so deactivatable and never deletable (`BR-TEN-036`).

`legacy` was minted for exactly one row, `government`, by a PO ruling that
explicitly declined to re-label it: *"a city water department and a state
university are different things and the stored value cannot tell them apart"*.
**Every write of it to date has been a migration's.** Since 2026-09-17 the rows
are the tenant's own (*"utility can get their own account types"*), so a utility
could in principle want the same treatment for a code of its own — *stop
offering `Marina berth` on new accounts, keep billing the eleven boats that have
it.*

### The question

Nobody has ruled whether a tenant admin may set or clear `legacy` on the S8
card, and the two obvious answers are both defensible:

**(a) Yes, on any row.** It is the tenant's list; retiring a code from new
business without disturbing existing accounts is exactly what a growing utility
needs, and `active=false` — the only control they have today — is the blunter
instrument: it removes the code from filters and reports as well.

**(b) No, or only on rows the tenant created.** `government`'s legacy flag is a
PO RULING about a specific migration hazard, and a clerk clearing it would put
an unselectable code back on the new-account form in every screen at once,
silently undoing a signed decision. A per-row rule (*seeded rows' `legacy` is
the platform's; your own rows' is yours*) is a third shape and needs its own
sentence.

### What is built while this is open

The card **serves** `legacy` beside `active`, so a picker built on
`/lookups/account_types` can tell a retired code from a live one — closing the
half of `DEF-421` that said it could not. **No control writes it**, and
`AccountTypeLookupHandler` says so in its own docstring rather than leaving the
absence to be discovered. A utility that needs a code off the new-account form
today uses `active=false` and accepts the wider effect.


## OQ-RAT-12469 — with a LIST of customer classes on a plan, is a charge code offered when it fits ANY of them or only ALL? (`DEF-RAT-5768`, 2026-09-19)

**Status:** 🟡 **OPEN — and BUILT AS `ANY`, deliberately, rather than stubbed.**
A stub here would be a blank step 4 on every plan, so the lane took the reading
that cannot hide anything and filed the question instead of burying it. If the
PO answers `ALL`, the change is one predicate in `addableCharges` and one case
in `planWizardBetaWalk.dom.test.tsx`.

**WHAT THE RULING DOES AND DOES NOT SAY.** PO 2026-09-19, verbatim: *"your
understanding is correct - we have all option anyway in drop down list - that is
default"*, answering how a plan's single customer class becomes a list. That
settles the CARDINALITY and the DEFAULT — one class becomes a list of one, NULL
becomes `[]`, and `[]` means EVERY class. It says nothing about what *"does this
charge fit this plan's class"* means once a plan names several, and that question
is read by `addableCharges` on step 4 of the plan wizard, which turns the draft's
classes into CODES and matches them against `charges.applies_to_customer_classes`.

**THE TWO READINGS, WITH THE CASE THAT SEPARATES THEM.** A plan for Residential
AND Municipal, and a charge code scoped to `["commercial"]` only:

* **ANY** — a code is offered when it fits at least one of the plan's classes.
  A code scoped to `["residential"]` alone IS offered to the Residential +
  Municipal plan.
* **ALL** — a code is offered only when it fits every class the plan names. That
  same residential-only code is NOT offered, and a plan naming two classes can
  attach only codes scoped to both of them or to none.

**WHY `ANY` WAS TAKEN.** It is the reading that cannot HIDE a code a clerk can
see in the charge-code catalogue, and an offered code is still only a code a
clerk chooses — nothing is attached by being offered. `ALL` would mean that the
very case the PO described (one plan priced for two classes) can attach almost
nothing, because a utility that scopes its codes at all usually scopes them to
one class each. The safe direction here is the permissive one precisely because
the act is a human choosing from a list, not an automatic assignment.

**WHAT IT AFFECTS.** `addableCharges` in `07-frontend/src/features/rating/
PlanWizard.tsx` and nothing else — this is the picker's narrowing, not the
engine's. R4's own class narrowing prices against ONE account's class at bill
time and is untouched either way.

## OQ-RAT-12470 — does the `Rate schedule` column stay, when neither drawn frame carries it? (`DEF-RAT-5774`, 2026-09-19)

**Status:** 🟡 **OPEN.** Ours to decide and write down (hard-won law 13) — it is
not a signed figure and nothing collides with a ruling, so it is on the register
to be ANSWERED by the next lane in this module, not put to the PO.

### What is already settled, so the question is as small as possible

`DEF-RAT-5774` added the `RATE` column that **both** frames of the Plans & Rates
blueprint draw — p102 for the wizard's step 8, p107 for the plan's page — after
the code had recorded, wrongly, that *"a fifth column is not drawn on either
frame"*. Read as images (B14 rule 42) the frames draw:

* **p102 · step 8** — `SERVICE · BASE · USAGE · RATE`, four columns.
* **p107 · the plan's page** — `SERVICE · BASE · USAGE · RATE · CHANGE ALREADY
  DATED`, five.

**Neither draws the schedule's NAME anywhere in the band.** What shipped is
`SERVICE · BASE · RATE SCHEDULE · USAGE`, so the name occupies the slot the
drawn `RATE` belongs in. The fix ADDED `RATE` and left the name, which is five
columns on both screens and one more than p102 draws.

### The question

Does `Rate schedule` go, to match the drawing exactly, or stay?

**The case for keeping it is not sentiment, which is why this is a question and
not a cleanup.** That cell carries a distinction nothing else on either screen
draws: *no schedule* (the plan prices nothing for this service — a publishing
refusal) against *the catalogue page this screen read did not carry the tariff
the plan names*. Those are different facts and only one of them is a fault. Drop
the column and the second fact has nowhere to go.

**The case for removing it** is B14 rule 41 and `DEF-GOV-5248`: the blueprint
owns layout, and a column no frame draws is ours, not theirs.

### What must not happen

Removing it silently as tidying. It is a column a clerk reads, and the two
absences it distinguishes were each written for a defect. Whoever answers this
decides where the *unscanned* absence goes FIRST, and only then removes it.

### Where the answer lands when it is made

`04-docs/05-modules/06-rating/02-business-rules.md`, `12-governance/02-decision-log.md`,
this row's status AND its body, and the `scheduleRateValue` docstring in
`07-frontend/src/features/rating/PlanSummaryCard.tsx`, which cites this id.

## OQ-RAT-12473 — three sample plans lost the customer class they were written for. Here is what each one was. Please confirm. (`DEF-RAT-5823`, 2026-09-19)

**Status:** 🔴 **OPEN — and it is a one-word answer, not a piece of research.**
It is on this register rather than decided by us because re-stating a plan's
customer class changes which charge codes a clerk is offered, and because we
recovered the answer from old records rather than reading it off the plan. **We
are asking you to confirm three words, not to work anything out.**

### What happened, in plain English

On 17 September we changed how customer classes work: every utility now owns
its own list — Residential, Commercial, Industrial and so on — instead of
sharing one list across the whole platform. That change moved every customer
account onto the utility's own list correctly. **It missed the rate plans.**

So three of your sample plans are still pointing at the old, deleted list.
Nothing crashed and nothing said anything. What it looks like on screen is
this: where the plan should say *Residential*, it shows a 36-character
computer code instead — and the plan quietly stops limiting itself to one
class, so the wizard offers it every charge code there is rather than the
residential ones.

**We have now cleared those three broken values.** The screen no longer shows
a computer code. But a plan with no class means *"this plan is for every
customer class"*, and these three were each written for ONE. **That is still
wrong — it is just honestly wrong, and you can see it.**

### The three plans, and what each one needs

| Plan | What it is called on screen | What it says now | What we believe it should say |
|---|---|---|---|
| `SCW-RES` | Sample — Residential | *every class* | **Residential** |
| `SCW-COM` | Sample — Commercial | *every class* | **Commercial** |
| `SCW-IND` | Sample — Industrial | *every class* | **Industrial** |

### Why we believe that, and why we did not just do it

We did **not** guess from the plan's name. `SCW-RES` looking like *residential*
proves nothing — a plan code is a word somebody typed, and this repo has a
standing rule against reading a name as a fact.

We got it from your own accounts. When the class lists were replaced, every
customer account was moved from the old entry to the utility's own entry **of
the same name**. So we can look at which accounts used to point at each of the
three deleted entries, and see what they are called today:

* **63 accounts** that pointed at the first one are all **Residential** today.
* **12 accounts** that pointed at the second are all **Commercial** today.
* **1 account** that pointed at the third is **Industrial** today.

All 76 agree, with no exceptions in either direction, and none of those
accounts has had its class changed by hand since. That is strong — but it
comes from an activity log that gets cleared out on a schedule, so it is
evidence we can show you **today** and might not be able to show you next
month. That is the main reason it is in front of you now rather than quietly
applied.

### What we need from you

**Just say whether those three are right.** If they are, we set them and it is
done. If any of them is wrong, tell us the right one and we will set that
instead. If you would rather these sample plans stayed open to every class,
that is a perfectly good answer too — say so and we will close this.

### What is blocked meanwhile

**Nothing.** The plans work, bills are unaffected — no part of pricing reads
this field, it only narrows what the plan wizard offers a clerk — and the
computer code is off the screen either way.

A build can be waiting on the fire marshal without being held, and held without waiting on anybody. The Hold door is what ties them together, by using the Waiting-on column as its notepad. **WHY NOBODY SHOULD JUST GO AND CHANGE IT.** The preference is not an oversight: the list was redrawn on 2026-09-28 and the drawing deliberately folds the two facts into one cell as *Waiting · fire marshal*, which is also why the Waiting-on column was moved behind the column chooser. All three surfaces then say the same word, and *Waiting · someone* still appears for builds that really are waiting on a person and are not held. **(b) THE OTHER TWO CHANGE TO MATCH THE LIST.** The list keeps showing what a build is waiting on, and the build's page and the filter chip start saying it too. **OUR RECOMMENDATION: (a), AND IT IS ALSO MUCH THE CHEAPER.** (a) moves one line of the list — which of the two facts the cell prefers — plus its test, and nothing else in the product changes. (b) cannot be done on the filter chip at all without new work on the server: the list can only be filtered by STATE, and *waiting* is not one of the states — it is a separate column, which is the thing `OQ-371` is already open about. So (b) is a server change, a screen change and a new filter, to make two screens agree with one. (a) also keeps the drawing honest rather than reversing it: the drawn cell shows a build WAITING on a named person, and under (a) that is still exactly what it shows — what changes is only that a build somebody PAUSED stops borrowing that wording. ⚠ **AND THERE IS A SMALLER DECISION INSIDE (a) EITHER WAY:** when a build is both held and waiting on someone, does the row show one fact or both? | OQ-FLD-12797 | **WHICH CERTIFICATES DOES THE APP PIN, AND HOW ARE THE PINS ROTATED?** The app only talks to our server over TLS 1.3 and checks the server's certificate against **two pins** (design Security §4) — because *"a pinned app with one expired pin is a fleet that cannot sync"*. The design requires the rotation written down before the first pin ships (Security §7.2). That depends on where the product is hosted and who issues its certificates, which is still open with operations (B1 TD-14). **Worked:** if our server certificate renews every 90 days and the app pins that exact certificate, every handset not updated within 90 days stops sending work on renewal day; pinning the issuer's key plus a backup key survives renewals. **Options:** (a) pin the issuing authority's key and one backup authority's key, replaced through an app update at least 60 days before either expires; (b) pin our own key plus a pre-made backup key, rotated by hand on a written calendar; (c) no pinning in the first release. **Recommendation: (a).** | eng+product | 2026-10-21 · lane DOC-C (`CR-187-BRC10`, T-64) · design: Security §4, §7.2 | The first store build that turns pinning on (T-57); the pin set in `field-app/src/security`. B3 addendum 2026-10-21 §4–§5 | CLOSED 2026-10-24 — (a) issuer + backup issuer, rotated ≥60 days before expiry, the pin set held in Settings › Security, not hard-coded. PO: *"plese dont hardcode it use settings"* (decision log 2026-10-24 (3)). |
| OQ-FLD-12798 | **SIGN-IN ON THE HANDSET USES TWO KEYS — MAY A HANDSET HOLD THE 36-HOUR ONE, AND WHO SIGNS OFF THE SERVER HALF?** Design ADR-026 (AD-21), rule R113, Security §1: a **1-hour** key to talk to the server, and a **36-hour** key locked to the device that lets the app keep recording work with no signal and signs each item. When the 1-hour key runs out, **sending** waits — recording never stops. ⚠ **THE SERVER HALF DOES NOT EXIST YET** — issuing and renewing the 36-hour key and checking each item's signature against the registered device (the device register exists; one or two columns and an endpoint are new). The design requires the model agreed with the owner of server sign-in before code relies on it (Security §7.1). **Worked:** Dana signs in at 07:30 and loses signal at 08:00; her 1-hour key runs out at 08:30 and she keeps working all day; at 17:10 on depot wi-fi she types her password and her 62 items send. If her handset is stolen at 12:00, a thief who got past the phone's passcode and the 5-minute lock could record work on it until 19:30 the next day — and nothing they record reaches the server without a password. **Options:** (a) as designed, 1 hour / 36 hours; (b) a shorter capture key, e.g. 14 hours (one shift), at the cost of a password prompt for anyone starting before their previous sign-in plus 14 hours; (c) one key only — rejected by the design because its expiry would stop the work. **Recommendation: (a).** | product+eng | 2026-10-21 · lane DOC-C (`CR-187-BRC10`, T-64) · design: Decisions AD-21, Rules R113 / R127, Security §1, §7.1 | The device sign-in and capture-key endpoints (decision log 2026-10-21 conflict 6: *"new endpoints (device login, capture credential) go in their own small PRs"*); `field-app/src/security`.
